hints: Match the $x^2$ and $x$ coefficients to a squared linear expression; then correct the constant term.
walkthrough:
Complete the square on the quadratic expression $9x^2 - 6x + 6$:
$$9x^2 - 6x + 6 = (3x)^2 - 2(3x)(1) + 1 + 5 = (3x - 1)^2 + 5$$
where $a = 3, b = -1, c = 5$.

hints: The vertex is at $x = \frac{1}{3}$, so smallest $p = \frac{1}{3}$.
walkthrough:
The parabola opens upwards with its minimum turning point at $3x - 1 = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{3}$.
For $f(x)$ to be one-to-one on the domain $x \ge p$, the domain must begin at or to the right of the vertex:
$$\text{Smallest value of } p = \frac{1}{3}$$

Set $y = (3x - 1)^2 + 5$ and isolate $x$ on the domain $x \ge \frac{1}{3}$ (where $3x - 1 \ge 0$):
$$(3x - 1)^2 = y - 5 \implies 3x - 1 = \sqrt{y - 5}$$
$$3x = \sqrt{y - 5} + 1 \implies x = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{y - 5} + \frac{1}{3}$$
$$f^{-1}(x) = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{x - 5} + \frac{1}{3}$$

Determine the domain of $f^{-1}$ from the range of $f$ on $x \ge \frac{1}{3}$ ($y \ge 5$):
$$\text{Domain of } f^{-1}: \quad x \ge 5 \quad (\text{or } [5, \infty))$$

hints: Since the minimum value of $f(x)$ is $5$, $f(x) = q$ has no solution for $q < 5$.
walkthrough:
Because the minimum value of $f(x) = (3x - 1)^2 + 5$ is $5$, $f(x) \ge 5$ for all $x \ge \frac{1}{3}$.
Therefore, the equation $f(x) = q$ has no solution when:
$$q < 5$$
